$comment: THE ARTWORK CANVAS SET (042) — one definition per shape the platform accepts.
⚠ THIS REPLACES THE SINGLETON `banner-canvas.json`. That file declared ONE canvas, 1200×600 at
2:1, and the server refused anything else. A bento grid needs tall, wide and square tiles, and a
2:1 image cannot fill a tall tile without the cropping the contract forbids.
⚠ NOTHING MAY HARDCODE THESE NUMBERS. A literal width in a component, a script or a test is the
drift this file exists to prevent — and it has already happened once: customer-web never imported
the canvas at all, hardcodes `aspect-[2/1]` in three places, and a test PINS the violation.
⚠ VALUES ARE PROVISIONAL UNTIL THE BENTO IS BUILT (T055a). The STRUCTURE is settled; the numbers
are confirmed against the rendered grid at each breakpoint. Artwork attached before that
confirmation is refused or mis-shaped once they change, so do not attach any.
⚠ WHY JSON RATHER THAN TS. `scripts/gen-compose-theme.mjs` is plain Node ESM and cannot import a
TypeScript module; the back-office console needs these as numbers and cannot read a CSS custom
property. JSON is the one format both ends consume without build-tool coupling.
⚠ WHY NOT tokens.css. That file is the BRAND source of truth — colours, spacing, radii, typeface.
An image canvas is an asset constraint, not a style token, and filing it there would be a category

hero.$comment: The full-bleed banner. 2:1 matches the band's proportion at desktop.

tile-large.$comment: The bento's anchor tile — roughly square at desktop, so a square canvas.

tile-wide.$comment: The horizontal tile. 16:9 rather than 2:1 so it does not read as a second hero.

tile-tall.$comment: The vertical tile. The inverse of tile-wide, so one photograph can serve either.

tile-small.$comment: The paired small tiles. Square, and the smallest artwork the platform accepts.
